dk_asof.asof: latest snapshot with core_odds.observed_at_utc <= the quote's observed_at_utc and < kickoff and <= data cutoff
dk_asof.role: SECONDARY, decision-time clean, descriptive only (no verdict)
dk_asof.source: forward capture core_odds.providers entry with provider_id '100' (DraftKings) and is_live false; spread = home_spread_current, total = total_current

espn_close.role: PRIMARY, UPPER BOUND (the close postdates the quote); the verdict comes from this arm

rule.data_cutoff_note: Polymarket rows and DraftKings snapshots observed after the cutoff are ignored, and games with kickoff after it are not graded, so appends to the live files after registration cannot change the sample. Input sha256 values are recorded at run time.

grading.fee_note: no platform fee is modelled; P&L is at the executable ask only
grading.pushes: excluded (impossible at half-point lines; counted if ever seen)
grading.requires: integer home_score and away_score, status 'completed' or absent (history-appended rows carry no status but have final scores), kickoff before the data cutoff
grading.spread: home covers iff home_score - away_score + home_line > 0 (half-point line: no push)
grading.total: over iff home_score + away_score > line (half-point line: no push)

matching.method: normalise names (drop U+FFFD, NFKD accent strip, lowercase, '-' -> space, drop apostrophes, okina and periods, keep [a-z0-9()& ], collapse spaces, then the alias map). ESPN school = the longest prefix of the ESPN display name that equals a normalised Polymarket school name; the rest is the mascot. A Polymarket event matches the unique 2026 games.jsonl game whose two schools equal the title's two schools with |kickoff difference| <= window; zero or several candidates = unmatched.

rule.question: Do 2026 Polymarket NCAAF decision-time asks lag the sportsbook line enough to profit, net of the ask? Model-free: only the Polymarket rung at the anchor line is traded.

row_filters.description_check: spread: float(long.description) == line and float(short.description) == -line; total: long.description == 'Over' and short.description == 'Under'; rows failing are excluded
row_filters.kickoff: min(Polymarket event_start_utc over the event's rows, ESPN games.jsonl event_start_utc)

selection.both_sides_qualify: take the lower ask; exact tie -> the long side
selection.integer_anchor_treatment: NO PICK (counted). Every Polymarket rung is x.5, so no rung equals an integer anchor; a rung half a point away is not fair at 50% and interpolating needs a margin distribution.
selection.max_ask_justification: At a half-point anchor the fair price of either side is about 50%. 48c is fair minus the 2% minimum edge the NCAAF Main gate already uses (edge band 2%-8%, ROADMAP College Football item), so the threshold is the house minimum edge, not a fitted value. One value, no grid.
selection.rung: the full-game rung whose (home-oriented for spreads) line == anchor line exactly
selection.which_snapshot: the EARLIEST qualifying row by (observed_at_utc, market_slug)

side_mapping.spread: long = the event title's FIRST team ('A vs. B' -> A) covering at `line`; short = the other team at -line. home_line_of_rung = line if A is the ESPN home team else -line. The `team` field is an assertion only: a row whose `team` resolves to the OTHER team (by school name or mascot) is excluded; an unresolvable or ambiguous `team` (shared mascots) is accepted.
side_mapping.total: long = Over at `line`, short = Under at `line`

metrics: break-even = mean ask of the picks

verdict.arm: espn_close, spread and total pooled; by-market results are descriptive
verdict.small_n: if the pooled arm has fewer than 30 graded picks or fewer than 5 date clusters the verdict is INCONCLUSIVE whatever the CI says (a bootstrap over a handful of clusters is degenerate)

rule.volume: espn_close arm picks per ET Saturday, over Saturdays (ET kickoff date) with at least one kept full-game rung of an event that has an ESPN close anchor; Saturdays with no valid capture or no ESPN anchor are listed separately and not in the mean

volume.note: the espn_close anchor exists only for games before the 2026-11-15 ESPN fetch, and Saturdays whose full-game rows are all timestamp_valid false have no kept rung
